newsitem.title: GERMANY: VW sees 102 percent rise in 1996 earnings.
newsitem.headline: VW sees 102 percent rise in 1996 earnings.

text.p: German carmaker Volkswagen AG said on Tuesday group earnings rose 102 percent to 678 million marks ($404.5 million) on the back of a 13.6 percent rise in sales to 100.1 billion marks.

The carmaker said it would propose to its supervisory board that the dividend on 1996 results for ordinary shares be raised to nine marks per share from six marks in 1995 and to 10 marks on preference shares from seven marks.
The dividend payout would equal 318 million marks.
Profit at the group level rose to 678 million marks from 336 million marks in 1995, while earnings at the parent level rose 54 percent to 630 million marks from 410 million marks.
But the carmaker said cash flow, viewed by analysts as a more transparent look at VW's health, rose a meagre 4.4 percent to 10.85 billion marks.
The carmaker has been famous in the investment community for providing limited information about its books and profit figures have long been considered heavily influenced by provisions and taxes.
Stock traders were unimpressed by the results, saying the profit figures were below market expectations and shares in Volkswagen slipped 5.00 marks in post-bourse electronic dealings to 791 marks.
The 30-share DAX index was up 54.17 points at 3,234.80 points, or up 1.70 percent, in the IBIS dealing session.
